To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cutting time, temperature and the amount of calcium chloride used in cheese making affect curd moisture content and curd yield and that the rate of expulsion of whey from curd is dependent on temperature and calcium chloride level.
cutting the gel at a firmness that is neither too soft nor too firm, and using the right level of calcium, will result in the best curd quality and yield.

curd moisture content is a function of the rate at which water is expelled from the gel during syneresis, which is a function of temperature; curd yield is a function of calcium chloride level, temperature, and cutting time; and curd fat losses are a function of cutting rate, temperature, and curd moisture content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model to predict cheese quality and quantity from the coagulation and syringesis process.
the study of the effect of cutting time, cutting temperature, and calcium addition on curd moisture and fat retention.
the development of a new methodology for monitoring cheese making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
response surface methodology is a useful tool to study the effect on cheese making of several factors that are difficult or impossible to control simultaneously.
the response surface methodology approach was successful in determining the optimal cutting time, temperature and calcium level for curd moisture, fat losses, and yield.
the optimum cutting time is a function of temperature, calcium chloride level, and the rate of gel coarsening.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the response surface methodology can be used to optimize cheese-making process.
the cheese-making process can be optimized using a combination of response surface methodology and optical sensors.
we have developed a model for curd moisture content and curd yield that can be used to optimize these 2 important cheese-making parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response of light backscatter can be used to predict cheese quality and yield, and the response of the optical sensor can be used to control the process.
the use of sensors to monitor cheese-making processes can help in the optimization of the process and in the development of new products.
the use of response surface methodology in conjunction with in-line optical sensors can be used to optimize the curd moisture, fat retention, and curd yields of cheese.
